p:cNvPr.descr: A diagram shows the process of FRAP. At the top of the diagram is an oval shape with the membrane visible. The cell is simply outlined with blue and lined with blue on the inside, with yellow in between. The center is plain white. It is labeled “cell” and a white arrow points up and left to a segment of a phospholipid bilayer with blue heads and yellow tails. Below, a down arrow has text to the right that reads “React cell with fluorescent probe to label lipids.” Below this is the original cell with the membrane still intact; it is now outlined with red. This is the fluorescent probe. To the left is an arrow that points to a segment of the bilayer with red dots above it, representing the probe. It is labeled “fluorescent probe on lipids.” To the upper right a white arrow points to a square full of red dots with text reading, “View surface with fluorescent microscope.” A down arrow below points to the cell outlined with the red probe and a red wavy line inside a pink rectangle (the laser) is attacking the right side of the cell. Above it is text reading, “Intense laser beam bleaches small area.” A white arrow points to the upper right, where the box full of red dots now has a large white hole in the center, which is the bleached area. A final down arrow below points to the cell outlined with the red probe. The arrow has text on the right that reads, “With time, unbleached phospholipids diffuse into bleached area.” A white arrow points up and right and shows red phospholipids moving into the white bleached area.
